summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent abdominal pain and suspected sphincter of Oddi dysfunction presented with acute epigastric pain and nausea after eating, following a reported lipase elevation to 713 at an outside hospital. Upon arrival, her lipase was 96, within her baseline range. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and pain control. An ERCP with biliary sphincteroplasty was performed, showing no stones or blockages but successful dilation of the biliary duct, leading to symptom improvement. She advanced to a regular diet, remained stable, and was discharged home on a short course of ciprofloxacin with instructions to continue her prior medications. Her abdominal pain, nausea, diarrhea, headache, and psychiatric conditions were monitored throughout the stay, with no complications.
